short: The eleven controls, their item shapes, the day, locale and link mints, and the row stepper
is: The shipped controls (Button, IconButton, TextInput, Select, Checkbox, Toggle, Tabs, ScrollingTabs, PillSwitch, Menu and DateField), one Svelte file each with its spec beside it; the plain TypeScript item shapes they take (`types.ts`) and the mints for a link, a calendar day and a language tag; two internal helpers (FieldFrame, Tooltip); `floating.ts`, which picks where a floating part is put; `step-row.ts`, which steps a scrolling row one item at a time; and `pill-type.ts`, which finds the one type a switch's typed options share.
conventions: One `.svelte` file per control, its `X.svelte.spec.ts` beside it. FieldFrame (lays out the label, hint and error) and Tooltip are internal: neither is exported. Item shapes and mints are plain TypeScript next to the components.

Props are readonly and typed: no `$bindable`, no rest props, no `$props()` that is not destructured. TextInput takes only its listed native attributes and no `id`. Callbacks carry plain values (`onPress()`, `onChange(id)`, `onCheckedChange(boolean)`, `onOpenChange(boolean)`, `onSelect(id)`), never a DOM or bits-ui event.

A control is controlled and keeps no copy of the value. A bits-ui root takes function bindings, Select's included; TextInput binds `value` with a getter and a setter; Checkbox calls back, waits a tick and writes the prop back; DateField takes its value through a derived date and keeps only its segments as interaction state. A parent that refuses a change leaves the control showing its prop, and every stateful control has a spec for that.

Typed ids are generic. A string coming back from the page is looked up in the options, never cast; an unknown or empty one is ignored. A hidden input renders only when `name` is given, and Select's only once a value is chosen. Every control takes a `testid` for its interactive element. A busy Button sets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, keeps focus and ignores presses.

Every word a control shows is a prop, the words bits-ui supplies for the date field's segments included; the one exception is the date announcer's "Empty". A label is text, never markup. `words.spec` reads the real components for a literal word.

Motion only through the seam. A control calls `useEnvironment()` once at init, puts `squish` on every pressable element but Select's trigger, which lifts as a field does, and `note` on the floating element that takes bits-ui's content props, and plays cues (`toggle` for Checkbox, Toggle, Tabs and PillSwitch; `open` and `close` for the menu and the select; none for buttons). It imports nothing from `lib/motion` and uses no `transition:`, `in:`, `out:` or `animate:`. With no provider it is still.

A floating part (the menu, the select's list, the tooltip) keeps bits-ui's two levels: the wrapper that carries the position stays unstyled and the inner element takes the note. It portals into the nearest `data-skin` element, else the body, so it wears the skin it opened from, and it opens only through an entry interaction, never at load. Opening focuses the menu without scrolling any box around it.

bits-ui and `@internationalized/date` are imported only by `.svelte` files under `src/lib`, and no type from either crosses the public API. A spread attribute is allowed only on an HTML element, and only when it spreads the `props` or `wrapperProps` of the nearest `{#snippet child(…)}` that only bits-ui can render: the snippet sits right under a bits-ui component, or is handed to one as `child` and used nowhere else. IconButton may also hand its snippet to Tooltip as `trigger`; Menu alone hands its snippet to Tooltip as `trigger` and spreads that snippet's `props` onto `DropdownMenu.Trigger`, the one spread allowed on a component, which then holds only bits-ui's own `{#snippet child({ props })}`. Tooltip hands its trigger an exact set of keys, pinned by its spec.

Arrows on Tabs and PillSwitch move and choose. A release never chooses on its own: a menu row chooses on a click, and a select option on a release only after a press on that same option; Select forgets the press at every open, close, cancel and release. A menu stays open until a choice, Esc or a click outside. ScrollingTabs is the one composite: Tabs with two named, tipped step IconButtons, always shown and each disabled at its end; a step moves the tab list's own scroll by one tab (`step-row.ts`), never through `scrollIntoView`, and never changes the tab showing. Every other control is simple. Tabs render a panel only for the active tab. The date field picks a day and no time.
A control's looks are the family stylesheets in `../styles/controls`; a control writes no colour, time or size of its own.
